ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: French Monetary and Financial Code (Code monétaire et financier), Articles L.561-1 through L.561-50 and R.561-1 et seq., as amended by Loi n°2016-1691 du 9 décembre 2016 (Sapin II) and Loi n°2018-898 du 23 octobre 2018 (transposing Directive (EU) 2015/849 and Directive (EU) 2018/843); French beneficial ownership register (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs, RBE) created by Loi n°2018-898 and implemented by Décret n°2019-133 du 22 février 2019 and Arrêté du 27 juin 2019; supervision by TRACFIN (French Financial Intelligence Unit) and the Conseil de l'Ordre des Avocats for regulated legal activities.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of the passport and proof of residential address of each beneficial owner and proposed manager (gérant)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent notarial or municipal authority in the country of origin; notarized copy then legalized
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (for signatory states) OR French Consular Legalization (for non-Hague Convention states)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good conduct / police clearance certificate (extrait de casier judiciaire or foreign equivalent) for each proposed gérant
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National Criminal Records Office of the country of residence or Ministry of Justice; French equivalent: Casier Judiciaire National
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR French Consular Legalization, followed by certified French translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of existence / registration extract (certificate of good standing) for any corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Official company registry of the shareholder's home jurisdiction (e.g., Companies House, SEC, local commercial register)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR French Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney (procuration) authorizing the French depositary lawyer or agent to execute and file all incorporation formalities
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the country of origin or French notary/consul where executed abroad
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR French Consular Legalization on the notarial act

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Corporate resolution approving the establishment of the French subsidiary and designated authorized signatories (for corporate UBOs)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors or shareholders' meeting of the foreign corporate shareholder, lawfully notarized or certified
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR French Consular Legalization, plus certified French translation

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, managers, and authorized signatories against: (i) the EU consolidated financial sanctions list (Gel des avoirs, administered by DG Trésor); (ii) United Nations Security Council Resolution 1267/1988 sanctions regimes; (iii) French domestic restrictive measures under Articles L.562-1 et seq. of the Monetary and Financial Code; (iv) Politically Exposed Persons lists under Article L.561-10 of the CMF following TRACFIN guidelines; and (v) for any USD-denominated settlement or US correspondent banking channel, the OFAC SDN list. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory whenever a PEP, high-risk third-country, or sanction flag is identified, with escalation to the firm's AML compliance officer and, where required, a TRACFIN suspicious transaction report under Article L.561-15.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: INPI – Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises (https://formalite.entreprises.gouv.fr), with name availability verification via Infogreffe (https://www.infogreffe.fr) and the Registre National des Entreprises (RNE)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be written in Latin script and registered in the French national alphabet. All corporate documents in a foreign language must be accompanied by a certified French translation (Loi Toubon n°94-665 du 4 août 1994). The dénomination sociale may include foreign-language elements provided that a French inscription of the registered name appears in the RNE and that the name does not conflict with protected trademarks or cause confusion with existing registered entities. For regulated legal practice, the name must not falsely imply bar membership or official judicial authority.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Chambre de Commerce (when not officially authorized)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: French law does not operate a statutory free-standing name reservation outside the full incorporation file. Priority to the name is established at the moment the RNE registration is effective; the 30-day window reflects the period allowed for completion of the filing after initial submission, after which the file lapses and must be refiled. Upon a name rejection or identity conflict raised by the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce or by the INPI, file a formal written réclamation (recours gracieux) addressed to the Greffier en chef of the competent Tribunal de Commerce within one month of the refusal notification. If the rejection is maintained, appeal to the Cour d'appel within fifteen days of the re-notification (Article R.123-82 of the French Commercial Code). Where the refusal originates from the INPI/RNE check, lodge an opposition or complaint before the Directeur Général de l'INPI within two months of the notification, followed by an action before the Paris administrative court if necessary.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted: Article L.123-11-1 of the French Commercial Code allows a legal-registered office to be established at the premises of a licensed domiciliation company (centre d'affaires or pépinière d'entreprises) under a domiciliation contract. For ISIC 6910 (legal and litigation services), a fully virtual address without physical file-holding and client-meeting space may be accepted for the corporate back-office; however, if the entity operates as an officially registered law firm (avocat), the Bar Council (Conseil de l'Ordre) will require a physical office with confidentiality-compliant archives and meeting facilities as a condition of the legal practice authorization.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 0.20 – Moderate to high probability (estimated 20–25%) of an unannounced or spot on-site inspection within the first 24 months of registration. The risk is elevated for legal-sector entities owing to mandatory inspections by the Ordre des Avocats, periodic compliance audits by TRACFIN under the AML/CFT framework, and physical verification visits by the commercial registry or tax authorities where the registered office is a domiciliation address.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff applicable to the 'immatriculation d'une personne morale' under the Guichet unique decree (Décret n°2019-133 and INPI fee schedule)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce – registration and file-handling fee for SARL incorporation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (commercial registration division)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official tariff of commercial court registrars (Arrêté du 8 février 2023, inclusive of debourse and statutory dues)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal publication of the incorporation notice (annonce légale)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Authorized legal-announcement newspaper (journal d'annonces légales) in the department of the registered office
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutorily regulated per-line rate published in the authorized journals; average SARL creation notice (3–4 lines)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name availability research report (dossier de vérification d'identité et de disponibilité de dénomination)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Gref fees and electronic research delivery charges pursuant to the official tariff order

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified French translations of foreign-source corporate, UBO, and good-conduct documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Certified translator accredited with the Cour d'appel (traducteur assermenté)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market tariff per page (€40–60) applied to approximately 5 pages, including notarized attestation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille or consular legalization fees for four notarized documents

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory per-document fee (€30–40) charged by the issuing authority in the respective jurisdictions

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark in accordance with Article L.123-11-1 C.com., average for business-center domiciliation in Paris or major regional city

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal drafting of articles of association (statuts) and full incorporation formalities coordination

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Statutory books and registers (registre des décisions, registre des mouvements de titres) and corporate seal

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Articles L.223-1 et seq. (formation of SARL), L.210-2 (legal capacity), L.223-18 and L.223-19 (managers), and R.123-30 et seq. (registry registration); operational formalities under Décret n° 2023-12 on the Guichet Unique.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) — Tribunal de Commerce de Paris, operated through the national Guichet Unique des Formalités d'Entreprises (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Standard business formalities form (formulaire 'M0' or successor digital declaration) for application for registration in the RCS, submitted through the Guichet Unique portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No legal minimum capital for SARL; share capital is fixed freely by the articles (commonly €1). Any subscribed capital exceeding €0 must be fully paid up at subscription and, if in cash, lodged in a blocked escrow account with a French bank, notary, or the Caisse des Dépôts; the capital is released upon registration of the company with the RCS.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: Resolved that the founding subscribers hereby adopt the articles of association of FR_SARL in the form of a société à responsabilité limitée; that the share capital of €1,000 be and is fully subscribed and deposited in escrow; that the registered office situated at 1 Rue de la Paix, 75002 Paris, France be and is adopted; and that Mr. Jean Dupont and Ms. Marie Leclerc be and are appointed as co-Gérants, with power to act jointly and individually, with full powers to open banking and trust accounts, sign all legal and tax filings, appoint the statutory accountants, and take all necessary steps for registration and licensing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and authentification of memorandum of association and capital deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company founders, legal counsel, notary (for notarized articles), and selected French bank or notary for escrow deposit.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the 'Statuts' (articles) of the SARL, each associate must sign. If cash capital is subscribed, open a blocked professional account and deposit the capital therein under escrow instructions. Obtain a capital deposit certificate from the bank or notary. Notarization is optional unless real property contribution is made.
required_dossiers: Draft/executed articles of association (Statuts)
Capital deposit certificate or notarial attestation
Address justification for registered office (lease, domiciliation agreement, or notarial deed)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct deficiencies in the articles or obtention of supplementary documents; re-execute signatures; appeal to registry judge if a notary or bank refuses issuance of the deposit certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of legal announcement in a law-authorized gazette
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Authorized legal advertisements newspapers (e.g., Affiches Parisiennes / Petites Afficches) designated by the district competent for the registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the draft announcement text containing the company name, legal form (SARL), capital amount, registered office address, corporate object, duration, and managers' details. The newspaper publishes the announcement and issues an 'attestation de parution' legal proof.
required_dossiers: Text of legal announcement
Draft or executed statutes
Power of attorney for signature if filed by a third party
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Republish with the exact corrected information if the announcement is rejected or nullified; ensure publication within one year of drafting statutes to avoid penalty.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic submission via the Guichet Unique national portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Guichet Unique des Formalités d'Entreprises, jointly operated by the French State and private registry partners.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Access formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr, complete the unified company creation forms, upload all required documents, and choose the commercial court registry for RCS registration. The platform transmits the dossier to the relevant registry and tax/social authorities electronically. Pay the official fees online via regulated payment rail.
required_dossiers: Completed online formalities form
Executed articles of association
Capital deposit certificate
Attestation de parution (legal announcement)
Proof of registered office address
Identification documents of each manager and associates
Criminal record declaration / non-conviction attestation (pièce n°1)
Statutory declaration of managerial capacity and acceptance of duties
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to registry queries within the statutory deadline; resubmit the corrected dossier through the same Guichet Unique; if rejection is final, appeal before the President of the Commercial Court (juge de l'immatriculation).

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RCS registration and issuance of K-bis extract
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Registry of the Commercial Court) for the place of the registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The greffier examines compliance of transmitted dossier, checks formal legality, approves entry in the RCS, and issues the registrations extracts, including the 'extrait K-bis' constituting conclusively valid legal proof of incorporation and name/insured persons.
required_dossiers: Verified dossier transmitted by the Guichet Unique
Receipts of payment of registration fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Request an expedited review in exchange for a supplementary fee; if the greffier refuses, appeal to the Clerk of the Commercial Court and finally to the President of the Court within 15 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-registration tax and social identifier formalities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INSEE (SIRENE), Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP), URSSAF / MOA, and body social for the professional division.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After RCS entry, the company automatically receives a SIRET number through exchange of information from the registry; the tax office attributes a specific corporate tax number (numéro de TVA and SIREN). Professional liability insurance subscription must be evidenced to the bar council.
required_dossiers: K-bis extract
Articles of association
Proof of professional liability insurance coverage
Bank/procuration and account details
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Contact INSEE via the 'Sirene' hotline to expedite attribution; contact DGFiP local tax office to rectify fiscal number anomalies; implement correcting transfers at URSSAF as needed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Professional law practice licensing and bar admission
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Conseil National des Barreaux (CNB), Ordre des Avocats of the relevant court district (e.g., Barreau de Paris), and Bar Council of the applicable court.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply to the competent bar for inscription on the Roll of Lawyers (Tableau de l'Ordre) and, where the SARL practices as a corporate body, obtain approval to exercise law as a 'société d'exercice libéral' (SELARL). The bar verifies compliance with education, nationality, good conduct, insurance, and ethical rules; deliver the certificate of professional capacity.
required_dossiers: K-bis extract
Professional indemnity insurance certificate
Criminal record extract / attestation of probity
Law degree (Master en Droit / CAPA) and admission to professional examination
Declaration of compliance with bar regulatory requirements
Bank account details (Déclaration de compte professionnel)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bar denies admission, the applicant may appeal to the Court of Appeals (Cour d'appel) within 30 days of notification; produce corrected documentary evidence to the Bar Council to avoid delays.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Conseil National des Barreaux (CNB), Ordre des Avocats of the territorial jurisdiction, and, for the corporate form, the Legal Affairs Division of the Ministry of Justice (Direction des Affaires Civiles et du Sceau).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Registration on the Roll of Lawyers (Tableau de l'Ordre) together with authorization to operate as a société d'exercice libéral (SELARL) for the practice of law, plus mandatory professional liability insurance certificate.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Agence de la Transition Écologique (ADEME) for advisory support; statutory supervision by the Regional Environmental Authority (Autorité Environnementale) and DREAL Préfecture for any classified installation if the activities generate discharges.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt (office-based professional services do not trigger systematic EIA); the activity is not listed as a 'installation classée pour la protection de l'environnement' (ICPE) in normal operation, unless major fit-out works exceed thresholds requiring a separate environmental registration.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with the French Environmental Code for waste management: sorting and disposal of paper/cartridgés; negligible VOC emissions; local sewer discharge limits under Public Health Code (Art. R.1331-2); compliance with refrigerant management rules (F-Gas) for HVAC equipment; energy performance obligations (Décret Tertiaire) where applicable.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification for premises receiving the public (ERP) issued by the Commission de Sécurité if the capacity exceeds 100 persons or as imposed by prefectural orders; structure must comply with the French Construction and Housing Code load-resistance requirements; workplace clearance includes ergonomic inspection and verification of electrical installations and work equipment conforming to the Labour Code; disabled-access conformity is mandatory and subject to favorable opinion by the accessibility commission.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) via the impots.gouv.fr portal; business entity registration files are processed through the Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI) single digital window (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr) which assigns the SIREN/SIRET and triggers automatic VAT registration with the competent Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1) File incorporation dossier (M0/statuts/Kbis) with the INPI CFE portal to obtain SIREN, SIRET, and Code APE 6910Z; the DGFiP then automatically assigns the French intra-Community VAT number (format FR + 2-digit control key + 9-digit SIREN) and publishes it on the EORI/VIES registries. 2) For a foreign entity establishing a SARL branch or permanent establishment without separate incorporation, direct registration via form 1478-SD and a request to the SIE is required. 3) Obtain the professional license for litigation chambers (Ordre des Avocats / Bâtonnier) and the CARPA trust authorization, which is a regulatory prerequisite to operate the IOLTA_Trust_Account payment rail. 4) Validate the VAT ID through the VIES system and register for the French e-invoicing platform (Portail Public de Facturation) within the statutory delay. 5) Appoint a tax representative if invoicing French VAT when the SARL elects the non-resident simplified regime (not applicable to a resident SARL).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. A resident SARL is mandatorily subject to Impôt sur les Sociétés (IS) at the standard rate of 25% (reduced 15% rate on the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit for SMEs meeting the statutory size tests). The pass-through fiscal transparency regime (Impôt sur le Revenu under Article 239 bis AA CGI) is available only by election for small SARLs (fewer than 50 employees, annual turnover below EUR 10,000,000, shares held by individuals), and even when elected, the entity remains subject to VAT at entity level. Territorial scope: France has unitary national taxation; no French tax-exempt zone applies to a commercial litigation SARL, and the General Tax Code excludes legal services from the franchise en base de TVA exemption.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: 1) Pass-through election under Article 239 bis AA CGI for small SARLs eligible to be taxed as IR-transparent; option is filed with the annual return and is irrevocable for five fiscal years. 2) Election for IS taxation under Article 206 CGI for SARLs initially outside the IS scope (rare; not applicable where the entity is IS by default). 3) VAT grouping election under Article 256 C ter CGI allowing closely linked French entities to form a single VAT person (assujetti unique) with one VAT number and consolidated intragroup reporting. 4) ATAD 2 hybrid mismatch rules (Articles 209 B and 212 bis CGI) are mandatory, not elective; there is no US-style check-the-box election, and a French SARL cannot unilaterally reclassify itself to exploit hybrid mismatches. 5) Optional 3% payroll tax and CVAE/CFE local assessments elections are not relevant to tax identity.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée (TVA) — French Value Added Tax governed by Code Général des Impôts Articles 256–289, harmonized with EU Council Directive 2006/112/EC
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No turnover threshold for legal and litigation services: VAT registration is mandatory from the first French taxable transaction because legal services are expressly excluded from the franchise en base de TVA (Article 293 B CGI). The general small-enterprise VAT exemption thresholds of EUR 85,000 for goods and EUR 37,500 for services do not apply to this activity. For non-resident suppliers, the EU OSS distance-sales threshold of EUR 10,000 per calendar year applies only to B2C e-services/goods, not to B2B litigation services, which trigger reverse-charge VAT treatment in the customer's jurisdiction.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory structured e-invoicing is being phased in under the Loi de Finances 2023. All French B2B invoices must be issued and transmitted electronically through the Portail Public de Facturation (PPF) or a certified Plateforme de Dématérialisation Partenaire (PDP). Compliance dates: 1 September 2026 for large and mid-size enterprises (obligation to receive and issue), and 1 September 2027 for all SMEs (including the SARL). Accepted formats are Factur-X (EN 16931 hybrid), UBL, and CII over the PEPPOL network. Data completion is mandatory in real time for e-reporting of B2C and international transactions, including export zero-rated supplies. No digital stamping is imposed; the system relies on continuous electronic clearance of transactional data to DGFiP. Non-compliance penalties under Article 1737 CGI range from EUR 15 to EUR 15,000 per invoice, with graduated sanctions for failure to issue, transmit, or include mandatory fields.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Cross-border commercial litigation and arbitration services are zero-rated for French VAT on the export of services when the place of supply is located outside France under Article 259-1 CGI (B2B general rule: services supplied to a customer established in a third country are deemed supplied outside the EU and therefore outside the scope of French VAT, allowing 0% VAT invoicing with full input VAT recovery). Services to EU business clients are addressed by reverse charge (autoliquidation) in the client's member state, not by French zero-rating. Zero-rating is denied when: (i) the service relates to immovable property situated in France, (ii) the service is physically performed in France for a private individual (B2C), (iii) the client's French fixed establishment is the recipient, or (iv) the litigation exclusively concerns domestic French proceedings without an export substance; in such cases the standard 20% French VAT must be charged.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DAU - Document Administratif Unique) transmitted electronically via the DELTA export system evidencing the physical exit from EU customs territory
Bill of Lading (connaissement) or equivalent transport document (CMR consignment note, air waybill, or filed export manifest) proving the cross-border movement
Inward Remittance Certificate confirming the collection of export proceeds and foreign exchange repatriation
Client contract and engagement letter establishing the beneficial recipient's place of establishment outside France
Attestation de résidence fiscale / non-EU taxable person declaration (or VIES validation screenprint for EU clients) evidencing the client's status
Fee invoice endorsed with the statutory exoneration mention 'Article 259-1 CGI - Exportation de services'
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The DGFiP audits export zero-rating claims with strict economic-reality testing under Article 283-1 CGI, reviewing the actual establishment of the client, the delivery of the legal service, and the provenance of the remittance. On a successful challenge, the tax authority retroactively re-subjects the supplies to 20% French VAT with interest for delay (intérêts de retard at 0.20% per month). Statutory penalties apply under Article 1729 CGI: 40% for material inaccuracy or misstatement (insuffisance de déclaration) and 80% for fraudulent maneuvers or fictitious export schemes; input VAT credits claimed on related costs are simultaneously rejected under Article 1731 CGI. Criminal liability under Article 1741 CGI exposes directors to a fine up to EUR 500,000 and imprisonment up to five years for tax fraud. The abuse of law procedure (Article L.64 LPF) permits the administration to ignore sham export structuring, and in cases of fraud the clawback period extends to 12 years (Article L.186 LPF).
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_refund_substantiation: The 180-day FX repatriation deadline is computed from the due date of the receivable; the supporting Inward Remittance Certificate must be produced within the same period to sustain zero-rating. Failure to repatriate within 180 days without a justified waiver triggers automatic reassessment at standard rate plus penalties.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France), acting with the Direction Générale du Trésor of the Ministry of Economy and Finance for exchange-control policy and foreign-investment screening; prudential supervision is delegated to the ACPR (Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution); balance-of-payments statistics are administered by the Banque de France Direction des Relations Financières Internationales (DRFI); monetary policy and Eurosystem settlement are exercised through the European Central Bank.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France, as a Eurozone member, applies full current- and capital-account convertibility under Article 63 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union and Articles L151-1 et seq. of the French Monetary and Financial Code (Code monétaire et financier). There is no prior authorisation, no quantitative restriction, and no dual-rate exchange regime for euro conversions. Profit remittance for a French SARL is unrestricted after the ordinary shareholders' meeting, subject to (i) corporate income tax at 25%; (ii) the 12.8% dividend withholding tax reduced by treaty or the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive; (iii) the 17.2% social levies under the single flat-tax regime of Article 200A CGI; and (iv) the standard financial-reporting formalities. The only practical hurdles are the mandatory Banque de France statistical declaration for any cross-border transfer exceeding EUR 12,500 and compliance with EU/OFAC financial sanctions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France imposes no export-proceeds surrender, mandatory conversion ratio, or repatriation timeline. Eurozone membership and EU capital-movement liberalisation preclude any surrender or conversion obligation. The residual statutory requirement is purely statistical: every cross-border receipt (including legal-service export fees, settlement awards, and reimbursements of disbursements) exceeding EUR 12,500 must be declared to the Banque de France DRFI within 20 days after the end of the month of receipt. Export proceeds may be retained in the invoicing currency or freely converted at the market rate.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (compte courant) plus segregated Client Funds/Escrow Account (compte de séquestre) for litigation deposits and awards
Operational Account with multi-currency sub-accounts (USD, GBP, CNH) and Client Funds/Escrow Account for cross-border commercial litigation
Treasury and cash-management Account: operational current account, SWIFT MT103, commercial escrow, and foreign-exchange hedging
Operational Account with local-branch fiduciary services; limited multi-currency and escrow product depth
Operational Account only; no dedicated escrow, trade, or treasury services for cross-border litigation

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: LOW for client-fund escrow and regulated litigation deposits, MODERATE for operational disbursement accounts. French AML law and the statutory-licence obligations require IOLTA/CARPA-type client money to remain at a fully ACPR-supervised credit institution. A fintech may operate lawfully in France only under a French credit-institution licence or an EEA passport under PSD2 (payment institution) or the E-Money Directive; offshore digital EMIs without a French/EEA branch or authorised agent cannot hold client funds, provide French IBAN-clearing, or substitute for the regulated escrow account. Qualifying French/EEA fintechs such as Qonto, Treezor, or Mangopay are acceptable for operational expense flows but must not be used for the segregated litigation-client account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: French AML/CFT rules require the bank to identify the legal entity, its legal representatives, and the beneficial owners registered in the RBE (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs). A physical interview of the gérant is generally required at the branch; since 2021, fully remote onboarding is permissible where the bank deploys an ANSSI-certified remote-identification solution with liveness detection and an eIDAS-notified electronic identity. In practice, BNP Paribas and Société Générale require one physical meeting of the SARL's legal representative and the presentation of original statuts, the RBE certificate, the statutory professional licence for legal activities, and identity documents. Remote opening for escrow-class accounts is not standard and will normally demand the added signature of the corporate-compliance officer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial-owner opacity: the SARL is held by corporate nominees, a foreign trust, or a chain of non-resident holding companies without a clear natural-person control structure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Evidence bundle: (1) certified copy of the statuts and the M0 incorporation form; (2) current RBE beneficial-owner registration certificate issued within 3 months under Articles L561-45 et seq. of the French Monetary and Financial Code; (3) passport and proof-of-address for each natural person directly or indirectly owning or controlling 25% or more; (4) the shareholders' register and an organisational chart; (5) a French apostilled certificate of good standing for each corporate shareholder; (6) a sworn declaration identifying the personne physique who ultimately controls the entity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and high-risk-jurisdiction traffic: inbound escrow receipts from clients or counterparties domiciled in EU/OFAC-sanctioned states or FATF grey-listed jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Evidence bundle: (1) executed retainer agreement (convention d'honoraires) and conflict-of-interest clearance from the bar or relevant professional register; (2) the case mandate from the court or arbitral tribunal establishing the legal rationale; (3) client due-diligence file with source-of-funds and source-of-wealth documentation (bank statements, asset trail, corporate records); (4) automated sanctions/PEP screening records for the counterparty and the beneficial owner; (5) evidence of any necessary freeze or refusal where EU/OFAC regulations compel blocking, and a Tracfin déclaration de soupçon if irregularity is detected under Article L561-15.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual wire velocity: repeated large receipts followed by rapid onward disbursements to third-party foreign counsel or settlement counterparties, inconsistent with the firm's litigation pipeline.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Evidence bundle: (1) detailed memoranda of fees (mémoires d'honoraires) and disbursement schedules (débours et frais de justice); (2) the client mandate letters and case references; (3) the segregated escrow ledger and account-reconciliation report; (4) a cash-flow forecast and staged disbursement plan approved by the gérant; (5) the firm's annual financial statements demonstrating economic proportionality; (6) copies of the underlying Court orders or arbitral directions supporting each payment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Crypto-currency or unregulated payment rails: a client proposes settlement or fee payment through digital-asset exchanges, unlicensed money-service businesses, or non-bank value-transfer channels.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Evidence bundle: (1) an internal anti-crypto/AML policy statement signed by the compliance officer; (2) proof of DASP/PSAN registration with the AMF and ACPR if the firm offers digital-asset services under the PACTE law, or evidence of refusal of crypto receipts where no registration exists; (3) the client's fiat-bank source-of-funds history demonstrating the legitimate origin of any converted amounts; (4) procedures requiring digital-asset conversion solely through a French/EEA-regulated service provider with fiat proceeds moved strictly into the regulated escrow account; (5) the bank's written acceptance of the policy.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For a non-resident shareholder's capital increase, shareholder loan, or working-capital injection: route via SWIFT MT103 (or SEPA credit transfer for EUR) to the SARL's operational corporate account using the French IBAN format FR76..., the bank BIC, a UETR/end-to-end reference, and remittance narrative 'CAPITAL INJECTION / APPORT EN COMPTE COURANT / [SARL NAME]'. For a formal SARL capital increase the funds must first pass through a blocked account held with the bank, a notary, or the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations and remain immobilised until the statutory increase formalities are completed; the wire must be accompanied by the gérant's attestation of contribution (attestation de versement) or a notarial certificate. The transaction is exempt from prior FX authorisation, but the bank will apply the EU statistical purpose code for capital transfers and the SARL must ensure the Banque de France DRFI balance-of-payments declaration is filed for every transfer exceeding EUR 12,500; OFAC/EU sanctions screening of the sender applies.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outward litigation disbursements use the following clearing rails: (i) SEPA Credit Transfer or SEPA Instant for EUR payments to EEA-based courts, experts, bailiffs, and counsel, using IBAN-to-IBAN instructions with the invoice and case reference; (ii) SWIFT MT103 for cross-border USD, GBP, or CNH payments to foreign counsel, experts, and settlement counterparties, with UETR and a purpose narrative 'LEGAL PROFESSIONAL FEES / LEGAL DISBURSEMENTS / SETTLEMENT'; banks require the underlying invoice, the retainer agreement, and the Court or arbitral order where amounts are atypical; (iii) commercial letters of credit (SWIFT MT700/MT710) and standby letters of credit (SWIFT MT760) where a Court-ordered escrow or settlement guarantee so requires; (iv) TARGET2/RTGS for high-value euro transactions. Each outward transfer above EUR 12,500 is captured in the Banque de France BOP declaration, and the SARL must maintain a payment-support folder (facture, convention d'honoraires, bordereau de créance, judgment) for audit; a Tracfin déclaration de soupçon is mandatory where laundering indicators are present.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain-vanilla foreign-exchange forwards (change à terme) with the ACPR-licensed credit institution, documented under a standard ISDA or French Federation FX master agreement and limited to genuine commercial or escrow exposures
FX swaps (swap de change) for rolling short-dated liquidity and tenor management of multi-currency client-fund balances

Cross-currency swaps (currency basis swaps) for long-dated foreign-currency escrow positions, subject to EMIR reporting to an EU trade repository and margin requirements where a financial counterparty is involved
Purchased vanilla FX options (call/put, no naked short structures) in EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, or EUR/CHF for settlement contingencies in cross-border litigation

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) permitted only for non-deliverable or offshore currencies (e.g., offshore RMB/CNH, and certain emerging-market currencies) where the underlying litigation receipt is denominated in that currency; executed through the bank's FX desk under a 1998 ISDA FX Novation/NDF confirmation, with on-demand evidence of hedging capacity provided to the bank's risk department

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% standard corporate income tax (IS) rate for fiscal years beginning on or after 1 January 2022; 15% reduced rate on the first EUR 38,120 of taxable profit for qualifying SMEs with turnover below EUR 10 million.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced SME rate; Research Tax Credit (CIR) 30% of eligible R&D expenditure; Innovation Tax Credit (CII); competitiveness and employment tax credit (historic); partial exemption for qualifying foreign-source income under French tax treaties.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Indefinite carryforward; annual deduction capped at EUR 1,000,000 plus 50% of taxable income exceeding EUR 1,000,000.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065 (liasse fiscale) and annexed schedules, filed electronically through EDI-TDFC on impots.gouv.fr or via certified EDI partners.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For 31 December fiscal year-end, file by the second business day following 1 May; for off-calendar year-ends, file within three months after the close of the fiscal year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total taxable income (résultat imposable) after depreciation, provisions and tax-elected adjustments; includes French and foreign-source income computed using the statutory rate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the French SARL's domestic profit; non-resident shareholders are not required to file this form or report a fiscal interest in the company on Form 2065.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign tax credits and tax-exempt income from foreign permanent establishments; supports the DTA credit method for foreign-source legal fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders may not claim this credit; the French company may offset foreign taxes only on its own foreign-source income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Research and Development Tax Credit (CIR) recapitulation; includes eligible expenses for proprietary legal-data analytics and litigation-management software.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only the French SARL may compute and claim CIR; the credit does not create a distributable dividend right for non-resident owners before liquidation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: International operations and foreign-company results schedule; captures permanent establishment dividends and controlled foreign source results.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders do not complete this schedule; payments to non-residents for services or royalties are separately reported on Form 2777.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty 10% within 30 days of formal notice, 40% beyond 30 days, 80% for abuse or strict refusal; late-payment interest 0.20% per month; EUR 150 per omitted annex schedule and EUR 15 per statement.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 30% French-source dividend withholding tax for non-resident recipients (Prélèvement Forfaitaire Unique); 0% under EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive for qualifying corporate shareholders holding at least 5% for 24 months; lower treaty rates may apply.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Prior to dividend payment, the non-resident shareholder must furnish a current tax-residency certificate (TRC), Form 5000, a beneficial-ownership declaration (Form 5001), and evidence of holding period; the French paying agent submits these to the DGFiP. If withholding is applied, a refund claim can be made directly to the local French tax office; anti-abuse and substance tests apply.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: domestic 33.33% withholding on French-source patent, trademark and software royalties paid to non-residents; treaty rates often 0% for software and industrial royalties and 0%-15% for artistic/trademark royalties. Interest: domestic law generally exempts French-source commercial interest; 75% withholding applies to payments to non-cooperative jurisdictions (ETNC); treaty rates typically 0%.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 3 million in intra-group transactions triggers the French Local File drawing obligation; consolidated group turnover or total assets of EUR 400 million triggers Master File and Local File preparation; Form 2257-SD transfer pricing declaration filing applies from the same thresholds.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: ESR in the Gulf/OECD sense is not directly applicable in France; however, French law requires genuine economic substance as a condition for treaty and EU directive benefits through Article L.64 LPF (abus de droit), Article 1655 bis CGI, and OECD BEPS Principal Purpose Test.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate under-declaration of fees from cross-border litigation, asset tracing or settlement recoveries; issuing sham invoices through shell affiliates; maintaining untaxed off-book assets or client funds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Corporation tax reassessment plus 80% abuse-of-law penalty (CGI Art. 1729); criminal fine up to EUR 75,000 and imprisonment up to five years (Art. 1741), increased to EUR 1,000,000 and ten years for aggravated fraud.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held civilly liable for corporate tax debts under the action en comblement du passif; criminal courts may impose travel bans, asset confiscation and imprisonment; French courts pierce the veil where the SARL is a mere instrumentality.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Incorporating and maintaining an SARL in France without premises, employees or local management solely to channel invoices, obtain French tax benefits or misapply EU treaty privileges.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment under Art. L.64 LPF with 80% penalty; refusal of treaty reduced withholding; cancellation of corporate registration; criminal exposure for fake corporate seat.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Civil restitution of misused corporate assets; personal bankruptcy (faillite personnelle), travel bans and director disqualification; creditors may seize personal property of shadow managers.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to perform client due diligence and file TRACFIN suspicious activity reports for cross-border settlement funds; commingling or dissipating IOLTA/trust monies held for foreign clients.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Monetary and Financial Code, fines up to EUR 15,000 for individuals and EUR 1,000,000 for legal persons; criminal imprisonment up to five years; Bar Council disciplinary withdrawal of license.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managing director personally responsible for segregated client funds; travel ban and asset freeze after criminal indictment; civil liability for conversion of client money and disgorgement of fees.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Manipulating intercompany legal-service fees, super-profit royalties or settlement commissions; failing to prepare and submit the French Local File and Form 2257-SD after crossing EUR 3 million threshold; using low-tax offshore invoicing hubs.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax adjustment under Art. 57 CGI with 40% deliberate-misconduct penalty; late interest; administrative fine up to EUR 50,000 under Art. 1735 ter CGI for TP documentation failure.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false TP certificates face personal assessments to unpaid taxes if reckless mismanagement of the company treasury is shown; criminal penalties for false documentation; travel restrictions in serious fraud investigations.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to file the ultimate beneficial owner on the RCS beneficial-ownership register; hiding a foreign litigation fund manager or third-party investor behind a nominal shareholder in the SARL.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fine up to EUR 15,000 and six months imprisonment under Art. L. 561-3-2 CMF for beneficial-ownership non-declaration; automatic increase to AML penalties if concealed owner is connected to money laundering or tax evasion.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Nominee shareholders and directors are jointly liable; civil liability for restitution of hidden profits; travel bans and seizure orders may be issued against both the nominee and the actual beneficial owner.
